parts.note: a sharp reply is a short, curt one
a drop or plunge is a fall

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
'to a T' is an idiom meaning exactly, perfectly

explanation.surface: Someone sizing up a creature and declaring it precisely small.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'to a T' supplies TOAT; 'This animal's' reads as 'This animal is', with 's as the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoat is a small weasel-like mammal, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Witticisms made by individuals touring ship

parts.note: individuals are ones, single units

explanation.surface: Jokes cracked by passengers as they look round a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: One-liners are short jokes, a kind of witticism delivered in a single sentence.

clue.text: Take care of Spooner's dog — pointer

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words, so the opening letters of the two pieces change places

parts.note: a poodle is a breed of dog
a tip is a pointer, a helpful hint

explanation.surface: Instructions to look after a dog of the pointer breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointer' looks like the dog breed; it is a hint. Swapping P and T in POODLE TIP gives the old British farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Toodle-pip is dated British slang for goodbye, a parting phrase like 'take care'.

indicators.note: reviewed suggests the letters of these words are looked over again and reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A law being looked at again once someone has grumbled about it.
explanation.definitionFit: An act of parliament is a law passed by a legislature, which is what a statute is.

clue.text: Unremitting, supporting political party in need of a large workforce

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means sitting underneath, so this piece comes below the party

parts.note: Labour is one of Britain's main political parties
intensive effort is unremitting, never letting up

explanation.surface: A campaigner tirelessly backing a party that needs plenty of staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour-intensive work demands lots of workers relative to machinery or capital.

parts.note: re means concerning or touching on, as in business letters
a cap is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: Someone told to pass over a hat, or to brush against it.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise again, going over the main points.

clue.text: Perch in river, and ducks on banks of Scheldt

explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a perch where birds settle to rest, the same thing as a perch.

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard as spoken rather than as written

parts.note: an evildoer is a sinner

parts.note: a gift is a present
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.definitionFit: A presenter hosts a television or radio programme, so host is a synonym.

parts.note: to open is to begin, as a show opens
something old hat is out of fashion, simply out

indicators.note: in places the word for have inside the cheese

to own something is to have it

explanation.definitionFit: A brownie is a small square chocolate cake.

definitions.meaning: a hearing of a case in a law court
a try-out or experiment to see how something performs

explanation.surface: An audiology appointment checking someone's ears.

indicators.note: off means gone bad or awry, so these letters are put into a new order

indicators.note: before places the draw first, ahead of the winning piece

parts.note: a tie is a drawn game
a team that is up is ahead, winning

explanation.definitionFit: To tie up is to fasten or secure, as a boat is tied up.

clue.text: Four-letter word used by girl upset about temperature

parts.note: Margaret is a girl's name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Four-letter word' suggests swearing; here it is literal. 'upset' turns MARGARET into TERAGRAM, and 'about' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetragram is any word of four letters; the Greek root means four letters.

parts.note: agin is a dialect form of against
a monarch's court is the body of courtiers who attend them

explanation.surface: A fight to oppose the king's courtiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Agincourt was the 1415 battle in which Henry V's army defeated the French.

clue.text: Cleaner, by a stop, caught early bus

parts.note: a char or charlady is a British cleaning woman
a ban puts a stop to something
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady at a bus stop catching the first bus of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'early bus' reads as the first bus of the morning, but means an old-fashioned motor coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc is an old-style open motor coach used for outings, a forerunner of the bus.

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so these letters are broken down and reformed

parts.note: someone who goes up in the air for a trial, the answer to 11 across

parts.note: a run in a stocking is a ladder

parts.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
sure means certain

a lass is a girl or young woman

clue.text: Willing to study ending in Waverley
